learner_operation: Infer invertibility versus singularity from a real square-matrix premise, evaluate each of three theorem conclusions, and select exactly the true subset.

fixed_features.feature: Real square matrix, positive dimension, one premise and three conclusions
fixed_features.justification: The lesson theorem and every target source question share this conceptual workload; rectangular matrices require different implications.

fixed_features.feature: Moderate band and observed radio/checkbox response shapes
fixed_features.justification: Only moderate is supported. Keeping source bank shapes preserves response workload; correctness still varies across five radio subsets or seven nonempty checkbox subsets.
Conservative context within a finite family; these constants do not justify fixing truth assignments, and are not counted as meaningful variation.

answer_roles.role: Premise implying invertible or singular state
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Equivalent determinant, rank, column-space, null-space, or nullity premise; both statuses.
answer_roles.observed: Both statuses occur across the independent sample and in the batch. Same-conclusion controlled premise flip changes all truth values correctly.

answer_roles.role: Qualifying conclusion labels, count and position
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Change conclusion polarity and premise state; vary which and how many conclusions qualify. Source examples include one, two and three true conclusions.
answer_roles.observed: All seven permitted checkbox masks and all five bank masks per radio profile occur in 87 controls. The delivered batch repeats middle-only on both det/Col/pivot questions, and all three checkbox questions have exactly one true statement.

answer_roles.role: Radio choice order and equivalent premise wording
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Shuffle alternatives without changing mathematics; change to an equivalent premise without changing the conclusion subset.
answer_roles.observed: Radio positions vary, but are not counted as semantic variety. Native grading and rendered equivalent-premise pair preserve the selection vector. Actual UI may additionally reorder radio alternatives.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Select only the last visible checkbox.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Matches the uniform seven-nonempty-subset baseline of 1/7; no evidence for this overall layout shortcut.

shortcut_probes.cue: Three checkbox concepts: determinant, column space, pivot columns
shortcut_probes.subgroup: Both members of this repeated family in the exact surviving runner batch
shortcut_probes.strategy: Select only the column-space checkbox, which is also the second visible field, ignoring signs and premise.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: 2/2 succeeds in the finite delivered subgroup, versus 1/7 for a uniform nonempty subset and 2/14 in fresh same-family controls. This demonstrates a batch-selection failure, not universal predictability of generate(). Actual UI preserves these checkbox positions; the concept cue also survives any field shuffle.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: 14 independently sampled members of that family
shortcut_probes.strategy: Select only column space, ignoring the premise.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: 2/14 equals 1/7; the generator can defeat the batch shortcut when its decision cases survive selection.

shortcut_probes.cue: Checkbox layout in exact runner batch
shortcut_probes.strategy: Predict that exactly one box must be checked.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: The count cue is correct for 3/3, compared with 3/7 singleton subsets in the seven-case control domain. This predicts only response size and is supporting evidence; the demonstrated full-answer shortcut is the two-item column-space subgroup.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: Independent samples containing a basis conclusion
shortcut_probes.strategy: Reject a no-basis assertion; accept a has-basis assertion.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Every finite-dimensional null space has a basis, including the empty basis. This uses the mathematical content of the proposition; it is not an incidental cue. The 0.5 baseline is a random Boolean response, not an estimate of the sampled key distribution.

delivery.result: All 87 controls and all five batch records survive actual delivery filtering. The two-item shortcut subgroup survives unchanged. Learner selection does not inspect or rebalance true subsets, so it cannot guarantee removal of the weakness; its precise live draw is unavailable.

limitations: Captured inventory is basis 5418; future inventory, learner histories and active policy weights are not supplied. Exact live learner order/probabilities are not claimed.
The failure is confined to a recognizable two-record subgroup of the reviewed finite five-item batch; the larger generator domain has counterexamples.
One incomplete source radio case lacks a key, solution and valid correct bank option; canonical example lacks fields. No missing source bank was invented.
No finite audit proves absence of every shortcut. The independently seeded 87 controls cover all response masks, not every premise/status combination within every profile.
